title: Window Cleaning Software: The Tools a Window Cleaning Company Needs to Book More Routes
html:
Window cleaning software is the set of tools a window cleaning company uses to quote jobs, schedule routes, send invoices and track repeat customers. Most window cleaning companies need four: a CRM, route scheduling, quotes with invoices, and call tracking. Repeat customers are the profit in this trade, so start with the tool that keeps them booked. This guide covers what each tool does and how to choose, so your window cleaning marketing turns into booked jobs.

What does window cleaning software do?

Window cleaning software keeps one-time customers turning into repeat customers. A route business lives on recurring visits, so a missed reminder or a lost quote hurts more than one slow week. The table shows what each tool handles.

Tool What it does Needed when Check before you buy
CRM Stores every lead, quote and repeat schedule Leads come from calls, forms and door hangers Can it tag one-time and recurring customers?
Route scheduling Books crews and groups jobs by area You run more than one route a day Does it plan by neighborhood?
Quotes and invoices Prices by pane count or home size and takes payment Quotes take too long to send Can customers approve online?
Call tracking Shows which ad or page produced a call You pay for ads or local SEO Does it send data to the CRM?

What should a window cleaning CRM include?

A window cleaning CRM should record each customer with the home, the service and the repeat interval. That record turns a one-time quote into a recurring route.

  • Customer type: one-time, quarterly, twice a year or commercial.
  • Service detail: interior, exterior, screens, tracks or pressure washing add-ons.
  • Quote status: new, quoted, booked or lost, with a reason for lost jobs.
  • Rebook reminder: a text before the next cleaning is due.

A window cleaning CRM earns its fee when it turns one visit into a schedule.

What should window cleaning route software do?

Window cleaning route software should group jobs by area so crews spend time on glass, not on the road. Weather delays make rescheduling a daily task, so test that part first.

  • Jobs are grouped by neighborhood on the day view.
  • Crews see the address, the pane count and any gate notes on a phone.
  • Customers get a reminder and a rain delay notice.
  • Recurring jobs repeat on their own interval.

How do you choose window cleaning software?

Choose window cleaning software by testing three things: fit for your routes, fit for your crews and fit for your data. Run a short trial with a real week of jobs.

  • Fit for your routes: it handles recurring jobs and weather moves without rebuilding the day.
  • Fit for your crews: a new helper can read a job on a phone without training.
  • Fit for your data: it records the lead source and lets you export every customer.

What mistakes should you avoid when buying window cleaning software?

The most common mistake is buying a tool built for one-time jobs when your profit is in repeat visits. Slow crew adoption is the next one.

  • Choosing from a demo that has no recurring customers.
  • Ignoring weather reschedules, which happen all season.
  • Skipping the lead source field, so you cannot see which channel books work.
  • Picking a tool crews will not open on a ladder.
  • Locking customer data into a product you cannot export from.

What data should window cleaning software track?

Window cleaning software should track the few facts that explain growth. Those are the repeat interval, the lead source and the quote result.

  • Lead source, from call, form, door hanger, referral or repeat customer.
  • Service type, pane count or home size.
  • Repeat interval and the next due date.
  • Quote amount and whether the customer accepted it.
  • Whether you asked for a review after the cleaning.

How does window cleaning software fit with your marketing?

Window cleaning software organizes the demand that your marketing creates, and it cannot replace it. A good CRM with no traffic has nothing to track, and traffic with no CRM leaks leads.

Most window cleaning companies build both sides together. A fast site with a quote form, local search and ads bring in the calls, and the software keeps each customer on the route. Start with the tool that fixes your biggest leak, then connect it to the channel that feeds it.

What is window cleaning software?

Window cleaning software is a set of tools that help a window cleaning company quote jobs, schedule routes, send invoices and track repeat customers. Some products bundle these jobs together, and others handle one job each. Choose the tools that match how you book work today, then add more as you grow.

It should group jobs by neighborhood, show the address and pane count on a phone and send reminders before each visit. Check that it handles rain delays and repeats recurring jobs on their own. A tool that cannot reschedule quickly costs a crew hours every storm.

How much does window cleaning software cost?

Prices vary by product, number of users and features, so check each vendor's current price page before you decide. Compare the monthly fee, any setup charge and what happens to your data if you cancel.
